annotations.text:
Pick a direction, then I build it in Blade + Sass.

All three keep the accessibility work intact: risk is never colour alone (icon + text label), targets stay above 44px, and everything is sized for 375px.

Webfonts can't load inside this preview, so each artboard names the typeface it would actually ship with and shows the nearest system fallback.

Mixing is fine — e.g. C's type scale with A's palette.

Low-fi wireframes.

Grey bars stand in for content text; real text appears only on controls, tabs and labels — the things a reader needs in order to understand the structure.

The prose in section 4.2 carries the reasoning, so nothing is annotated here.

System diagrams.

4.5 and 4.6 use Yourdon & DeMarco notation: circles for processes, rectangles for external entities, open-ended rectangles for data stores.

4.7 (ERD) is not here — you already have it.

4.8 places each of the nine security elements (a)–(i) at the boundary it defends, and the legend below matches the lettering in section 4.4.1.
